guidance.source_quote: Therefore, at the total company level, revenue should be between $96 and $97.1 billion or growth of 18 to 19%.
We expect revenue from Agents and Infra of $80.1 to $80.7 billion, or growth of 24 to 25%.
In Azure, we expect revenue growth of 49 to 50% in constant currency
In M365 Commercial cloud, we expect growth of approximately 19% in constant currency
M365 consumer cloud revenue should grow in the low-teens, down sequentially as we lap the price impact noted earlier.
Microsoft Cloud gross margin percentage should be roughly 65%, down year-over-year
In devices and consumer, we expect revenue to be $15.9 to $16.4 billion.
Windows OEM and Devices revenue should decline in the mid-thirties.
We expect COGS of $32.7 to $32.9 billion, or growth of 26 to 27%.
And operating expense of $18.5 to $18.6 billion or growth of 9% driven by continued investment in R&D compute capacity and talent.
Operating margins should be down slightly year-over-year.
other income and expense is expected to be roughly negative $300 million
And we expect our Q2 effective tax rate to be approximately 20%.
In Q2, we expect CapEx spend will be over $50 billion.

reported.source_quote: This quarter, revenue was $92.3 billion, up 19%.
Earnings per share was $4.89, an increase of 18% and 19% in constant currency, when adjusted for the impact from our investment in OpenAI.
Revenue from Agents and Infra was $76.8 billion and grew 25%, reflecting strength across the connected layers of our platform.
Now to Microsoft Cloud. Revenue was $63.9 billion and growth accelerated to 30% and 31% in constant currency
Azure revenue was ahead of expectations and increased 48%, even with the 3P capacity delays noted earlier, driven by Foundry and improved CPU monetization.
Now to devices and consumer. Revenue was $15.5 billion and declined 3%.

reported.metric: Windows OEM and Devices revenue growth
reported.source_quote: And Windows OEM and Devices revenue decreased 22%.
Commercial remaining performance obligation grew 73% to $677 billion
Cash flow from operations was $58 billion, up 29% driven by strong cloud billings and collections.
Capital expenditures were $45.2 billion, as some third-party capacity deliveries we expected in Q1 were delayed.

tone.summary: Demand still exceeds the capacity Microsoft can supply.
tone.source_quote: Customer demand continues to exceed available supply.

tone.summary: Copilot daily users are growing quickly.
tone.source_quote: Daily users are up nearly 50 percent quarter over quarter, and over 5X year over year.

tone.summary: Delayed third-party GPU contracts push capacity into H2.
tone.source_quote: In Azure, we expect revenue growth of 49 to 50% in constant currency with continued efficiency gains across our CPU and GPU fleet helping to offset some 3P GPU as a service contracts that have been delayed to H2.

tone.summary: Weaker sales execution in E3 and standalone products.
tone.source_quote: Results were ahead of expectations driven by stronger GitHub Copilot adoption and usage, partially offset by weaker sales execution in our M365 E3 and standalone SKUs.

tone.summary: Windows OEM revenue missed on tough comps, channel destocking and weak PCs.
tone.source_quote: Windows OEM revenue was below expectations and decreased 27% and 28% in constant currency driven by the Windows 10 end of support demand in the prior year, inventory drawdowns by OEM and channel partners, and weaker PC market demand.

tone.summary: Cloud gross margin is falling as the mix shifts toward Azure.
tone.source_quote: Microsoft Cloud gross margin percentage declined year-over-year to 66%, driven by sales mix shift to Azure, partially offset by product-level margin improvements, primarily in Azure.
